holidays.name: National Increase Your Husband's Dowry Day
holidays.description: A tongue-in-cheek observance that invites people to ponder the old tradition of dowries, and to joke about whether anyone's spouse might be worth a little extra. It's mostly an excuse for humorous banter and a look at marriage customs through history.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial, humor-driven observance listed in quirky holiday calendars. Its exact creator is unknown, and it spread through novelty-calendar listings.
holidays.funFact: Dowries have existed for thousands of years, with records of them in ancient Mesopotamia, and in some places the custom persists in modified forms today.

holidays.name: National Chicken Cacciatore Day
holidays.description: A day to dig into the rustic Italian-style dish of chicken simmered with tomatoes, onions, peppers, mushrooms, and herbs. Home cooks and restaurants alike celebrate with big, saucy, comforting plates.
holidays.origin: Cacciatore means 'hunter' in Italian, and the dish began as a hearty meal for hunters in the Renaissance era. The food holiday is a modern addition to American food-day calendars.
holidays.funFact: The original hunter-style dishes were often made with rabbit or game rather than chicken, since hunters cooked whatever they caught.

holidays.name: National Mushroom Day
holidays.description: A celebration of fungi in all their forms, from button mushrooms on pizza to fancy morels and fearsome-looking truffles. Fans cook mushroom-heavy dishes and appreciate the strange organisms that are neither plant nor animal.
holidays.origin: Observed in the United States as a food-focused day promoted by mushroom enthusiasts and growers, tied to the autumn season when many wild mushrooms sprout.
holidays.funFact: The largest living organism on Earth is often said to be a honey fungus in Oregon, covering nearly 2,400 acres underground.

holidays.name: Global Handwashing Day
holidays.description: An international awareness day that encourages people everywhere to scrub up with soap. Schools hold hand-washing songs, glitter experiments, and demonstrations to show how germs spread.
holidays.origin: Founded in 2008 by the Global Handwashing Partnership, with the United Nations General Assembly year designated that same year as the International Year of Sanitation.
holidays.funFact: Washing hands with soap can reduce diarrheal disease by roughly 30 percent, making it one of the cheapest and most effective health measures ever.

holidays.name: White Cane Safety Day
holidays.description: A day recognizing the white cane as a symbol of independence for people who are blind or visually impaired, and reminding drivers and pedestrians to give right of way to cane users.
holidays.origin: Proclaimed by US President Lyndon B. Johnson in 1964 after a joint resolution of Congress, building on earlier advocacy by blindness organizations.
holidays.funFact: The white cane's use as a mobility tool is credited in part to James Biggs of Bristol, England, who painted his cane white in 1921 to be more visible to traffic.
